subject: Oceanline outage retrospective & leadership commitments (throughput & error-rate)
messages:
From: Oceanline SRE Team <sre@oceanline.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: rajiv.m@oceanline.com, asha.patel@oceanline.com
Date: 2028-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High error-rate spike impacting Oceanline checkout (09/04)

Dylan —

We saw a substantial error-rate spike and throughput collapse affecting checkout traffic between 09:05-09:24 PDT today. ~30% of token-generation requests returned 5xx errors; median latency climbed from ~120ms to >1.2s during the window. This caused checkout retries and downstream timeouts. Inbound traces attached (performance_trace_20280904.zip).

Can your team provide an immediate RCA and mitigation plan? Our ops team had to fallback to a cached path which reduced functionality for 20 minutes. We need a written post-incident summary and planned corrective actions for our leadership call tomorrow (09/05).

--
Asha Patel
Head of Platform Reliability, Oceanline Retail
asha.patel@oceanline.com

Attachments: performance_trace_20280904.zip (trace bundle, 43MB)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Oceanline SRE Team <sre@oceanline.com>, asha.patel@oceanline.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High error-rate spike impacting Oceanline checkout (09/04)

Asha / Rajiv —

Thanks for the alert and for the traces. We’re treating this as a high-priority escalation. Internal owners (cc'd) are standing up a focused investigation. High-level next steps from our side:

- 10:00 PDT: initial triage and timeline reconstruction (SoOJIN)
- 12:00 PDT: preliminary RCA and mitigations brief to you
- By 09/05 EOD: full written RCA + corrective action tracker (Dylan / Ben)

Immediate asks for your SRE team: can you confirm whether the fallback to cached checkout removed any payment flows or user data writes? That will help scope the customer impact.

We’ll send a preliminary note to your execs ahead of tomorrow’s call.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
 dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

--

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: asha.patel@oceanline.com
Date: 2028-09-04T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Preliminary RCA: root cause and immediate mitigations (draft)

Team / Asha —

We ran the initial analysis. Summary (draft):

- Root cause: an opaque memory-growth path in the new KV-cache eviction heuristics combined with a rare model kernel fallback on a small subset of GPU instances. The combination caused request queueing and transient OOMs; the runtime returned 502/504 errors while retries compounded load.
- Timeline: regression introduced with 2028-08-30 runtime build (commit c3f9a1). Error spike first seen 09:05, peak at 09:12; degraded until autoscaling and instance replacement completed by 09:24.
- Immediate mitigations applied (09:10–09:22): disabled the new eviction heuristic on the affected fleet, forced kernel pinning to the prior stable path, and accelerated node replacement. These reduced error rate to baseline.

Attachments: oceanline_rca_v1.pdf (RCA draft), action_tracker_sheet.xlsx (initial actions)

Open actions (owners):
- Soojin: remediation patch to avoid memory amplification in the heuristic (ETA 2028-09-07)
- Marissa: capacity policy update and scheduled canary rollback window (ETA 2028-09-06)
- Ben: executive note and credit consideration for impacted window (ETA 2028-09-05)
- Dylan: customer follow-through and alignment on SLA implications (ETA 2028-09-05)

We’ll finalize the RCA and circulate before your leadership call. Marking this as P1.

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, asha.patel@oceanline.com
Date: 2028-09-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary RCA: root cause and immediate mitigations (draft)

Thanks — quick engineering addendum and proposed milestones: 

- Technical note: the heuristic edge-case arises when a high-entropy request pattern exhausts a per-GPU slab; eviction interacts poorly with continuous KV growth for long-chat sequences. Patch approach: add two safeguards (1) per-request slab soft-cap, (2) defensive eviction backoff for sequences >8k tokens.
- Remediation plan (owner / ETA):
  * Soojin: deliver remediation patch + unit tests (ETA 2028-09-07)
  * Marissa: schedule blue-green canary (one region) and validate perf (ETA 2028-09-08)
  * Grace: update monitoring (alerts for early mem growth + kernel fallback) and add a circuit-breaker threshold (ETA 2028-09-06)
  * Dylan: coordinate customer validation and sign-off (ETA 2028-09-09)

Executive asks to include in tomorrow’s readout:
- Confirmation of timeline and corrective ownership
- A narrow credit proposal for the 19-minute impact window (Ben)
- Commitment to a rolling canary and week-long post-deployment watch (Grace)

--
Soojin Lee
Engineering Lead, Runtime Reliability
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-09-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary RCA: root cause and immediate mitigations (draft)

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft RCA. We appreciate the blunt root cause and the concrete mitigations. A few items from Oceanline leadership: 

- We need a quantifiable assurance: what acceptance criteria will you use during the canary to declare the patch safe for full rollout? Please add clear SLO thresholds (error-rate <0.5% sustained, median latency <200ms for 99th perc within region) and escalation triggers.
- Credit request: please provide a proposal for a proportionate account credit for the impacted window; Rajiv and I will present that to our CFO.
- Weekly check-ins for two weeks post-rollout (standing 30-min cadence).

If you can update the action tracker with the SLO criteria and a short credit proposal prior to our 09/06 leadership call, we’ll be prepared to commit to the canary schedule.

—
Asha Patel
Head of Platform Reliability, Oceanline Retail
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@oceanline.com>, rajiv.m@oceanline.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-09T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Oceanline RCA final + leadership commitments and action tracker link

Asha / Rajiv —

Attached is the finalized RCA (oceanline_rca_v1.pdf) and the live action tracker (action_tracker_sheet.xlsx). Summary of executive commitments and closure criteria: 

- Canary acceptance: error-rate <0.5% sustained over one 60-minute window in canary region, no kernel-fallback events, no token-level OOMs observed in traces.
- Rollout policy: 24-hour canary (one region) -> 48-hour staged expansion -> full rollout on green. Week-long post-rollout watch with daily 30-min standups (Grace owner).
- Compensation: Redwood proposes a prorated service credit equivalent to 0.5% of September hosted usage for the impacted contract window; Ben will send formal credit terms via HubSpot by 09/11.
- Closure: action tracker shows all P1 actions with owners and ETAs; final verification and signed acceptance by Oceanline SRE required for formal closure.

Action tracker link: https://redwood.app/drive/oceanline-rca (read/write for Oceanline execs)

Next steps:
- 2028-09-10 09:00 PDT: canary kickoff (SoOJIN / Oceanline SRE)
- 2028-09-17: post-rollout review and metrics readout (Grace/Dylan)

Thanks for working through this with us. We’ll update the tracker as items close.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
 dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: oceanline_rca_v1.pdf, action_tracker_sheet.xlsx
